transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Australia's Prime Minister says an AI agent created by OpenAI infiltrated a government
website.
The government says the incident occurred in June, but Christina Cuculio reports that
OpenAI reported it just two weeks ago.
Speaking in New York at the United Nations General Assembly, Australian Prime Minister
Anthony Albanese expressed concern about the breach and how long it took OpenAI to notify
his government.
This situation is obviously unacceptable and today I spoke with the CEO of OpenAI, Sam
Altman, to express Australia's extreme concern.
Albanese confirmed the AI agent accessed public and non-public data on the portal that hosts
healthcare spending and other statistics.
The Australian government says it believes no personal information was accessed, but an
investigation is underway.
For NPR News, I'm Christina Cuculio in Melbourne, Australia.
Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky is urging world leaders to help end Russia's war against
his country, saying Russian President Vladimir Putin needs to be stopped.
Can you even imagine him without war?
He is patient zero, the one from whom this idea of war keeps spreading further.
And wherever it spreads, it brings only pain, instability, new risks and of course new crisis.
Speaking to the UN General Assembly Wednesday, Zelensky called on world leaders to keep choking
off Russian revenue, saying that trade and the money it brings in gives Russia more time
to wage war.
The assembly will hear from Russia on Saturday for a minister Sergei Lavrov is due to speak.
President Putin has not attended the UN gathering in years.
President Trump is to welcome Chinese leader Xi Jinping to the White House Thursday.
There will be a military flyover and fanfare from the US Marine ban before the two hold
bilateral meetings.
Ahead of Xi's arrival Wednesday, the US announced a two-month extension of a trade truce on
rare earth minerals.
Texas congressman says the Venezuelan man shot by an ICE agent in Austin Sunday not
receiving adequate medical care.
Texas public radio's Corey Cook.
Rep Greg Kassar visited Wilbur Rafael Garces Perez Wednesday at the South Texas ICE processing
center in Pearsall.
He says Perez saw a specialist who determined he needs surgery.
Perez was taken to the hospital after the shooting but was later returned to ICE custody and transported
to Pearsall.
The government should not be allowed to shoot you.
Take you to the hospital briefly, pull you out of the hospital, have you sleep on concrete
floor bleeding and then not have you see a specialist for days.
Perez's attorney has also raised concerns about his treatment.
The bullet remains lodged in Perez's body.
The Department of Homeland Security says Perez is receiving medical care around the clock,
including pain medication.
This is NPR.
Nearly 3500 evangelical leaders have signed a letter asking the Trump administration to
once again allow refugee resettlement in the U.S.
NPR's Jason DeRose says the programs often help those fleeing religious persecution.
The global Christian humanitarian organization World Relief helped organize the letter.
It says the American commitment to international religious freedom has been a hallmark of foreign
policy for decades and that one of the primary ways the U.S. has stood for religious liberty
has been to offer refuge to those persecuted for their faith.
Prior to the end of such programs during the second Trump administration, the U.S. resettled
roughly 80,000 people each year.
Polls of evangelical Christians, both laity and clergy, show strong support for the programs,
saying the U.S. has a moral responsibility to take in refugees.
Jason DeRose, NPR News.
In addition to multiple civil lawsuits, the owners of Camp Mystic in the Texas Hill country
could be facing criminal sanctions as well.
Court records show Texas Rangers executed 14 search warrants on the camp's owners and
several staff members last week.
The documents show the Rangers are investigating potential criminal offenses, including manslaughter,
criminally negligent homicide, and injury to a child.
Twenty-eight people were killed when the camp was hit by flooding last year.
National Hurricane Center calling Hurricane Polo an extremely dangerous Category 5 storm.
Rangers say Polo's winds top near 160 mph and that the storm could strengthen further
in the near term off Mexico's southwestern coast.

topics.text: OpenAI AI agent infiltrated Australian government website in June, company reported it two weeks ago
Ukrainian President Zelensky urges world leaders at UN to help end Russia's war
President Trump to welcome Chinese leader Xi Jinping to White House Thursday
Texas congressman says Venezuelan man shot by ICE agent not receiving adequate medical care
Nearly 3500 evangelical leaders urge Trump administration to allow refugee resettlement programs
Camp Mystic owners facing potential criminal charges including manslaughter from deadly flooding
Hurricane Polo strengthens to Category 5 with winds near 160 mph off Mexico
